extracted.intended_audience: scholars, practitioners, and prospective visiting researchers interested in First Amendment issues (especially relating to technology)
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the Knight Institute’s research program expectations and topical priorities for scholarship and essays about the First Amendment, with emphasis on interdisciplinary work and technology-related issues. Signals the Institute's approach to hosting visiting scholars and publishing pieces that enrich public debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary scholarship and commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: The Knight Institute’s research program aims to foster interdisciplinary scholarship and commentary about the First Amendment, particularly on issues relating to new technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Institute hosts visiting fellows and scholars from multiple disciplines and publishes essays representing a broad range of perspectives. The research program explores a broader array of questions than the Institute’s litigation and policy work, complementing those activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide space for positions different from the Institute
rubrics_metrics.description: Through our research program, we explore a broader array of questions, and we afford scholars and practitioners the opportunity to develop and present positions that are sometimes different from our own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This pluralism is intended to enrich public debate and deepen the Institute’s own understanding of the First Amendment; the program explicitly welcomes work that may not reflect the Institute’s official positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of published pieces: well-argued, well-informed, and provocative
rubrics_metrics.description: We aim to publish pieces that are well-argued, well-informed, and provocative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions and published essays should demonstrate rigorous argumentation, informed factual and legal grounding, and be thought‑provoking; these are the stated editorial standards for pieces appearing in the research program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical relevance to program initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Research and essays should engage with themes the Institute highlights, such as strengthening free expression to protect democracy, the role of lawyers in preserving democratic freedoms, regulation of speech through federal funding conditions, and cross-border issues like surveillance and censorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Featured projects and essay series include 'Reconstructing Free Expression', 'Lawyering Without Law: The Legal Profession in an Age of Authoritarianism', 'Federal Funding and the First Amendment', and 'Regardless of Frontiers: The First Amendment and the Exchange of Ideas Across Borders' — work aligned with these topics is especially relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation as visiting fellows and scholars from multiple disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: The program hosts visiting fellows and scholars from multiple disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective participants should expect an interdisciplinary environment; the program highlights current and former visiting scholars and affiliates and maintains a Visiting Research Scholars program (links referenced on the page).
